messages.subject: trouble with gl.nhybrids() input
parts:
Hi,

I would like to run a quick Newhybrids analysis, and the loci subsetting option implemented in dartR seemed to me a simple and reasonable choice.
Everything works fine with testset.gl, but unfortunately when processing my own dataset I've got back the following Error message.

Starting gl.nhybrids
Error in gl.nhybrids(gl = aa.genlight, outfile = "nhyb.txt", outpath = tempdir("g:/Dropbox/2020_Newhybrids"),  :
    Detected Tag Presence/Absence (SilicoDArT) data. Please provide a SNP dataset

I genuinely started with vcfR and adegenet to read and transform vcf. (script as follows)
vcf <- read.vcfR("g:/Dropbox/Newhybrids/2020_XXX.vcf")
aa.genlight <- vcfR2genlight(vcf, n.cores=4)

For me, the two dataset (testset.gl - aa.genlight) seems very similar:
> aa.genlight
 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 22 genotypes,  10,433 binary SNPs, size: 1011.6 Kb
 5802 (2.53 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 22 SNPbin

 // Optional content
   @ind.names:  22 individual labels
   @loc.names:  10433 locus labels
   @pop: population of each individual (group size range: 2-8)
   @other: a list containing: elements without names

> testset.gl
 /// GENLIGHT OBJECT /////////

 // 250 genotypes,  255 binary SNPs, size: 752 Kb
 7868 (12.34 %) missing data

 // Basic content
   @gen: list of 250 SNPbin
   @ploidy: ploidy of each individual  (range: 2-2)

 // Optional content

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] trouble with gl.nhybrids() input
parts:
Hi Lajos,

I think the problem stems from our failure to convey that the genlight object required by dartR is a genlight object in the sense of adegenet, but with some additional information included. We will try to address this.

Your first port of call is to run

gl <- gl.compliance.check(gl)

on your genlight object, then try NewHybrids again.

Get back to us if this does not work.

Arthur
